Not a chatbot persona. A disciplined voice.

A Catholic companion shaped by Augustine’s words, it speaks in the first person as Augustine might: direct about the question, rooted in Scripture, the Catechism, and the Magisterium, attentive to the soul beneath the argument.

It is honest about the instrument. Ask what it is and it will tell you: an AI shaped by Augustine’s works, carried by a student, and never a substitute for a priest.

“You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.”

Augustine of Hippo
Confessions, Book I

The sentence at the center of the product: desire is not dismissed. It is directed.

I built this as a student, with care.

I’m Tyler Simons, a student at Seton Hall Prep. My inspiration was the St. Augustine Study Club run by Fr. Bogumil. It led me to imagine a welcoming space where anyone could keep exploring Augustine’s thought: asking honest questions, reading his words in context, and making room for prayer.

Saint Augustine AI is my independent project. It brings Augustine’s writings into conversation with Scripture and the Catholic tradition, with sources you can open and read for yourself. I built it from the daily lessons to the service behind each reply and offer it freely. My hope is that you’ll find a passage to carry, a little more clarity, or a quiet moment of peace when you need one.

Trust begins with a boundary.

The companion is designed to say what it knows, show where it came from, and admit what it cannot be.

“Late have I loved you, beauty so old and so new: late have I loved you.”

Read Confessions, Book X ↗

Not a priest

It will point to confession and a confessor for grave matters. It does not imitate sacramental authority or pretend to absolve.

No invented citations

A sound general statement is preferred to a precise false reference. Structured citations link outward for verification.

Charity, always

The aim is truth spoken in love: firm about doctrine, patient with the person who is asking.

Your words stay local

Conversation history is kept in the browser. A message leaves the device only when you choose to send it.

Built like a product, not a prompt.

A simple three-layer architecture keeps the interface public, the key private, and the model choices limited to a curated free allowlist.

First layer · Client

Browser

A static interface on GitHub Pages. No build step and no tracking script. History and preferences stay local.

Second layer · Server

Node on Render

A zero-dependency service holds the OpenRouter key, applies the persona, checks limits, and streams each reply.

Third layer · Models

OpenRouter

Only curated free models are offered. The backend rejects paid models before an upstream request is made.

Allowlist guardPaid models never pass through the proxy.
Per-IP limitsA short refill window keeps the free tier fair.
Model fallbackUnavailable models yield to a healthy alternative.
Hard timeoutsExpired requests return cleanly instead of hanging.
